finding: Durable provider-intent/replay safety requires a stable conversation key before the first provider call. The exact current key is client_metadata.thread_id or session_id. ConversationSegmentStore.get/put intentionally become no-ops for key=None. Therefore a Responses request without thread_id/session_id cannot publish V22/V28 provider intent, cannot recover exact replay after restart, and cannot safely execute a tool-producing provider turn under the new crash contract. The synthetic bridge probe explicitly supplies thread_id, but the real Codex CLI project probe only validates end behavior and currently does not prove what metadata the actual Codex binary sends on the wire.
required_invariant: Before any provider-entering ordinary Responses or compaction operation, durable Core mode requires a non-empty codex_conversation_key derived from stable client metadata.

If stable conversation identity is absent, fail closed before provider entry; do not invent an identity from request body, turn_id, random UUID, connection state, or process-local cache because tool-result continuation/restart must resolve to the same durable namespace.

The bounded real Codex acceptance probe must capture/sanitize the incoming request metadata and prove that the actual target Codex build supplies a stable thread_id or session_id across initial turn, tool-result continuation, retry and process restart. No secret or owner prompt bytes may be recorded.
If the target Codex build does not supply a stable conversation id, add an explicit client-side bridge metadata mechanism before live acceptance rather than weakening durable replay safety.
interaction_with_v28: V28's provider_intents ledger is keyed by conversation_storage_key(stable_conversation_key). V29 is therefore a prerequisite for creating a new intent. Existing exact replay lookup may proceed only when the same stable key is present.
